deploy.help:
digital-employee deploy [package-path] [options]

  Validate and bind the exact employee package before any deployment effect.
  package-path defaults to the current directory; at most one positional path is allowed.
  --package is equivalent and cannot be combined with a positional package-path.

  Channel capabilities:
    available:            http (ready only after authenticated readback)
    preview / pending:    console | dingtalk (pending_external_action; never ready)
    unavailable:          lark | wecom
  Agent-native engines:  claude-code | qoder | qwen-code | codebuddy
  standalone-v1 engines: extractive | openai-compatible (legacy commands only)
  Runtimes:              agent-native (default); package-bound standalone-v1 is unsupported
  Languages:             {locales}
  Outcomes:              ready=exit 0; pending_external_action=exit 2; unsupported/failed/invalid=exit 1

Options:
  --package <path>    Package path (at most one positional path; the forms conflict)
  --channel <id>      Deployment channel
  --engine <id>       Engine supported and available for the selected runtime
  --runtime <id>      agent-native; use `digital-employee legacy ...` for standalone-v1
  --name <name>       Local deployment display name
  --locale <code>     Effective locale ({locales})
  --port <number>     Loopback HTTP port (http channel only; default 3000)
  --yes               Skip confirmations; requires channel, engine, and runtime
  --help              Show help without prompts, config writes, providers, or processes

Stable defaults:
  package=current directory; name=Digital Employee; locale=en under --yes.

Examples:
  digital-employee deploy
  digital-employee deploy ./my-employee --channel http --engine qoder --runtime agent-native
  digital-employee deploy --package ./my-employee --channel http --engine qoder --runtime agent-native --locale en --name MyBot --yes
deploy.recovery_deploy_interrupted: The deploy was interrupted before completion. Rerun the same command: it reads back the saved binding, verifies or cleans partial local state, and resumes to ready or reports the exact blocking step.
workspace.help:
Digital Employee workspace commands

Usage:
  digital-employee workspace init <directory> --template <id> [options]
  digital-employee workspace help

Templates: oss-maintainer

workspace init materializes a business workspace skeleton (organization.v1alpha1.json, workspace.json, positions/, context/) into a missing or empty directory. It never modifies a non-empty target.

Options:
  --template <id>   Workspace template to materialize (required)
  --locale <code>   Output locale ({locales})
  --json            Machine-readable output

Example:
  digital-employee workspace init ./oss --template oss-maintainer
workspace.help_init:
Usage: digital-employee workspace init <directory> --template <id> [--locale {locales}] [--json]

Materialize a workspace skeleton (organization.v1alpha1.json, workspace.json, positions/, context/) into a missing or empty directory.

Options:
  --template <id>   Workspace template to materialize (oss-maintainer)
  --locale <code>   Output locale ({locales})
  --json            Machine-readable output

org.help:
Digital Employee org commands

Usage:
  digital-employee org tree [workspace] [--json]
  digital-employee org apply [workspace] [--json]
  digital-employee org scope <position> [workspace] [--tool <name> | --context <path>] [--json]
  digital-employee org help

The workspace directory is the enterprise: every position is a directory under positions/ holding its employee package plus budget.json, and the parent-child directory relation is the reporting line.

org tree renders the reporting hierarchy; --json emits org-tree.v1.
org apply reads the positions/ directory tree (add = hire, move = change reporting line, delete = dismiss), validates it fail-closed (a hire without a fully allocated budget never takes effect), updates .digital-employee/org.json, appends the audit log, and recomputes permissions.
org scope shows a position's derived Context Scope and Authority Scope; --tool/--context evaluate one request against them.

Options:
  --locale <code>   Output locale ({locales})
  --json            Machine-readable output

Examples:
  digital-employee org tree ./oss
  digital-employee org apply ./oss --json
  digital-employee org scope issue-researcher ./oss --tool Read
org.help_tree:
Usage: digital-employee org tree [workspace] [--locale ...] [--json]

Render the reporting hierarchy of the organization model (.digital-employee/org.json, bootstrapped from organization.v1alpha1.json when absent). --json emits org-tree.v1. Read-only: nothing is written.
org.help_apply:
Usage: digital-employee org apply [workspace] [--locale ...] [--json]

Read the positions/ directory tree and apply it to the organization model: add a position directory = hire (budget.json must be fully allocated), move it = change the reporting line, delete it = dismiss (recorded in the audit log). Every validated change updates .digital-employee/org.json, appends .digital-employee/org-audit.jsonl, and recomputes .digital-employee/permissions.json. Invalid changes fail closed with the organization model unchanged.
org.help_scope:
Usage: digital-employee org scope <position> [workspace] [--tool <name> | --context <path>] [--json]

Show the Context Scope and Authority Scope derived for a position, or evaluate one request: --tool checks the Authority Scope allowlist (writes are default-deny), --context checks the Context Scope. Out-of-scope requests are rejected with a stable code and point at the owner.
org.apply_dismissed: Dismissed {position}; the removal is recorded in the audit log (no silent removal).
org.apply_done: Applied {count} change(s); organization model, audit log, and permissions updated.
org.scope_context_allowed: Context path {path} is within the Context Scope of {position}.
